verdicts.why: Names a temporary interruption of an activity with no attitude toward the one pausing or the activity.
Plain word for ceasing an action briefly; the sentences show it used for hesitation without any judgement of it.
Names the act of buying something plainly; no more loaded than 'buying'.
Names the thing bought without approving or disparaging it.
A figurative 'grip' or leverage on something; describes the advantage without judging who holds it.
Technical mechanical sense with no attitude at all.
Names a virtue (self-control) plainly, as 'courage' or 'discipline' do; the approval in 'disdain of all restraint' comes from the referent being a good thing, not from the word framing it.
A limiting rule or condition, named without taking a side on whether the limit is welcome.
The act of holding someone or something back, described neutrally.
The state of being physically held; an unpleasant referent but a plain word for it.
Approving: chosen over 'plainness' or 'bareness', it frames the lack of ornament as a tasteful, deliberate choice rather than a lack.
Plain measure of how big something is; 'deficient in size' judges the house, not the word.
Means largeness; a strong meaning, not an attitude beyond it.
A graduated measurement, as of clothing; purely descriptive.
Idiomatic 'the size of it' states the actual situation without praising or dismissing it.
A craft material; no attitude possible.
Marking a letter with a date is a plain clerical act.
Assigning a date to something (the start of a feeling, in the sentences) describes without judging.
Going on a date with someone is named neutrally; no approval or contempt attaches to the verb.
Having a steady relationship with someone, named plainly.
Stamping with a date is a mechanical act with no attitude.
'Deep in thought' says how far in, not whether that is good or bad.
To a great distance; a measure, not a judgement.
'Deep into the night' marks lateness without any attitude toward it.
